criteria.descriptor: Correctly characterizes forward vs reverse KL (mode-covering/zero-avoiding vs mode-seeking/zero-forcing) and maps each to the observed symptoms; correctly identifies off-policy teacher-forcing as the source of exposure bias and on-policy distillation (GKD) as the remedy; states temperature/dark-knowledge and T^2 scaling accurately. Full marks require no reversed KL directions, no invented mechanisms, and a correct note that reverse KL on student samples needs a policy-gradient objective.

Covers all requested facets: mechanistic diagnosis, divergence-direction choice, sampling-regime choice, temperature, capacity-gap mitigation, and a generation-based validation plan. Deduct for each facet omitted or only named without substance.

Justifies each design choice by its underlying mechanism (why forward KL over-smooths a small student, why reverse KL sharpens, why on-policy sampling removes the inference mismatch) and surfaces the trade-offs (diversity loss / mode dropping, JSD for early stability, over-high T), rather than asserting fixes without linking cause to effect.

Organized as diagnosis -> revised recipe -> validation, uses distillation vocabulary precisely (forward/reverse KL, dark knowledge, exposure bias, on-policy/GKD, SeqKD), and reads at a senior design-review register without rambling or hedging.

expected_answer_points: Identifies that the objective is forward KL (soft-target cross-entropy), which is mode-covering / zero-avoiding, and that a low-capacity student forced to cover all teacher modes over-smooths - explaining the bland/hedging outputs and the leaked mass that causes hallucination.

Proposes reverse KL as the fix because it is mode-seeking / zero-forcing (student concentrates on the teacher's dominant modes for sharper coherent generations, e.g. MiniLLM), and acknowledges the trade-off of reduced diversity / mode dropping.
Diagnoses exposure bias / train-inference mismatch from off-policy teacher-forced training, which is why offline loss looks fine while deployed generation degrades.

Recommends on-policy distillation (GKD): sample sequences from the student during training and score with the teacher; notes reverse KL over student samples needs a policy-gradient formulation (not plain backprop through sampled text).
Handles temperature correctly: soften logits to transfer dark knowledge (relative non-argmax probabilities), tune T, scale loss by T^2 to preserve gradient magnitude, and avoid over-high T.
Addresses the teacher-student capacity gap with a concrete mitigation (teaching-assistant / intermediate model, hidden-state/feature matching, or domain-curated prompt distribution).

Specifies a generation-based validation plan (win-rate vs teacher via human/LLM judge, task benchmarks, hallucination and degeneracy checks, diversity metric), explicitly noting KD/validation loss is an inadequate proxy.
common_pitfalls: Reverses the KL directions - claims forward KL is mode-seeking or that reverse KL causes the over-smoothing - inverting the core mechanism.
Prescribes only surface tweaks (lower the temperature, train longer, use more teacher data) without addressing the divergence direction or the off-policy/exposure-bias root cause.
Treats distillation as ordinary supervised fine-tuning on the teacher's hard outputs, ignoring soft targets / dark knowledge and thus missing why forward KL behaves as it does.
Proposes on-policy / reverse-KL distillation but forgets you cannot backprop through sampled student text and omits the policy-gradient (GKD-style) formulation, or misstates the objective.
Concludes the 7B student is simply too small for distillation to work, instead of adjusting the objective and data regime.
Declares success on the basis of low KD/validation loss, missing that token-level loss can look great while generations are bland or hallucinated, and provides no generation-based evaluation.
reference_answer:
Diagnosis. The recipe is token-level, off-policy distillation under a forward-KL objective. Two coupled properties explain the symptoms.

(1) Divergence direction. Forward KL D_KL(teacher || student) is mode-covering / zero-avoiding: it heavily penalizes the student for assigning near-zero probability anywhere the teacher has mass. A 7B student cannot represent the 70B teacher's full distribution, so it is forced to spread probability to cover every mode, becoming an over-smoothed, high-entropy model. That is exactly the bland, hedging, generic behavior; the same smearing leaks mass onto tokens the teacher barely supports, which surfaces as confident hallucination on the long tail. Reverse KL D_KL(student || teacher) is mode-seeking / zero-forcing: the student concentrates on the teacher's dominant modes, producing sharper, more coherent generations (the MiniLLM result). The trade-off is reduced diversity / dropped modes, usually acceptable for an assistant.

(2) Sampling regime. Training only on teacher-forced sequences is off-policy: at inference the student conditions on its own generated prefixes, a distribution it never trained on, so errors compound (exposure bias) - which is why offline loss looks fine but deployed generation degrades. On-policy distillation (GKD) samples sequences from the student during training and scores them with the teacher, removing the train/inference mismatch. Reverse KL on student samples is not directly differentiable through sampled text, so it is optimized with a policy-gradient / on-policy formulation.

Revised recipe. Objective: on-policy generalized KD - sample responses from the student, score token distributions with the teacher, minimize reverse KL (or a generalized JSD early on to stabilize training when the student is far from the teacher). Warm-start / curriculum with some teacher sequences (SeqKD) before going fully on-policy. Temperature: soften both logits with a tuned T to transfer dark knowledge (relative probabilities of non-argmax tokens) and scale the loss by T^2 to preserve gradient magnitude; avoid excessive T, which re-introduces over-smoothing. Capacity gap: if the 70B->7B gap hurts convergence, insert an intermediate teaching-assistant model or add hidden-state/feature matching, and curate the prompt distribution to the target domain.

Validation. KD/validation loss is a poor proxy - low token-level loss coexists with bland generations. Evaluate on held-out prompts with generation-based metrics: win-rate vs the teacher (human or LLM-as-judge), downstream task benchmarks, explicit repetition/degeneracy and hallucination/factuality checks, plus a diversity metric to catch mode collapse from reverse KL.
